## Triage: first touch → `domain:spec` · p3 · `pm:queue` · 2026-11-14T08:46Z

⛔ Not a claim.

- **Row:** a per-audience landing or group placement cannot name a navigation entry contributed by a module package, so an industry module can never be a role's landing page. This is a capability limit, not a wrong answer: the declaration is refused or ignored as documented. p3.
- The navigation contract decides it (spec plus runtime resolution). If the lane finds the docs promise this, it becomes a wrong-running p2.

## Seat: not dispatched — half of the ask re-opens a recorded maintainer ruling → `needs-user-decision` · 2026-11-14T19:05Z

⛔ Not a claim. The lane takes this card as soon as the shape is ruled.

- **What the card asks:** (1) a per-audience `landing[].item` may name a navigation entry a module package contributes (`navigationContributions`), checked after contributions are folded; (2) a contribution may declare a position relative to an app entry (`before` / `after` an id), within bounds the app allows.
- **Governing ruling:** #28022, ruling record 6545223246 (batch 2026-10-31 item 3, maintainer 「同意」 2026-10-31T15:12Z): **A** ruled, a landing list key on the app; **B not taken**: "reuse `navigationContributions` with a declared position, no new key". Part (2) is that declared position, now asked beside A rather than instead of it.
- **Part (1)** widens A: today `checkAppLandingItems` (`packages/spec/src/ui/app.zod.ts`) refuses at parse an `item` that is not the app's own entry, the referential integrity the `homePageId` tombstone demanded. A parse cannot see contributions, so naming a contributed entry moves that refusal from parse to the post-fold check (registry fold at boot/publish, `os build`), or trades it for a weaker one.
- **Options for the evaluation:** A: both parts; B: part (1) only, the referential refusal moved after the fold, (2) stays not taken; C: neither, the app keeps owning landings (status quo, the downstream app pre-declares groups and orders).
- **State:** `pm:queue` → `needs-user-decision`. Evaluation brief: `/mnt/project-files/pm-orders/spec/33234-decision-brief.md` (project share).

## Ruled: C (no change) · Fable evaluation thread · 2026-11-14T21:20Z

⛔ Not a claim. Written by the evaluation thread the spec seat opened for this card (brief `/mnt/project-files/pm-orders/spec/33234-decision-brief.md`); labels, the body's `Ruled:` line and the card's state are the seat's.

- **Ruling-ref:** the maintainer (Leehom) chose option **C 「不改」** at 2026-11-14T21:19:19Z on the decision 「裁定 #33234:模块贡献的导航条目能否成为落地页」 in this account's fleet project (decision thread `cmsg_01TenzsRopZj4jMbvjX8uz1XKbi11aY8SWRcPc43gTa4HY`, card `cmsg_01TenzsRopZj4jMbvjX8uz1X2urAufVvk5hC7JsAsmxj3R`). Option text verbatim: "保持现状。模块条目要当落地,只能排到最前,或由模块自带一个应用。同一应用里按角色落到模块条目的场景无解。"
- **What it rules:** neither part of this card is built. An app's `landing` keeps naming only the app's own navigation entries, refused at parse otherwise (`checkAppLandingItems`, #28022 ruling record 6545223246, letter A, stands as written). No `before` / `after` position on a contribution: #28022's B stays not taken. No landing key on a contribution either (option D below, the evaluation's recommendation, was not chosen).
- **What an author does instead:** a module whose audience needs its own landing ships its own app (ADR-0019 D3 as amended, #32585; HotCRM's Service app), or the app that owns the navigation declares the entry itself.
- **Left to the seat (not ruled by the tap):** the evaluation read, without running it, that part (2) is already expressible: a contributed entry keeps its `order` through the fold, the console sorts each level by `order` after the fold, and a contribution's `items` may carry a `group`. If the seat confirms that, whether the docs say so (and a pin holds it) is a docs-gap call of the seat's, not a contract change. Closing this card is the seat's hand-over to the maintainer.

## The evaluation the ruling was made on

Recommended D; the maintainer ruled C. Kept here whole so the options and readings are on the card.

## One-sentence problem

A customer who adds an industry module to a packaged CRM cannot make a sales rep open the app on the module's Sales Orders list, and believes the module cannot place its entry between two of the app's own entries.

## Background

- #28022, ruling record 6545223246 (letter A): the app gained `landing`, a list of `{ item, visible }`, first match wins. B ("reuse `navigationContributions` with a declared position, no new key") was not taken.
- `checkAppLandingItems` (`packages/spec/src/ui/app.zod.ts`) refuses at parse an `item` that is not an entry of the app's own `navigation` / `areas[].navigation`. A contributed entry is not part of the app being parsed, so it can never be named.
- The console already resolves a landing against the served (folded) trees: `ui/packages/app-shell/src/console/appDeclaredLanding.ts#resolveDeclaredLandingRoute` looks the id up in the trees the member is shown, and passes over an entry it does not find.

## Governing text

- ADR-0130 §1.5: "navigation crosses only through contributions". A package's own `app.navigation` pointing at a foreign object is rejected; a contribution into a foreign app is accepted. `grep -n "navigation crosses only through contributions" docs/adr/0130-release-artifact-as-co-ownership-boundary.md`
- ADR-0029 D7: `navigationContributions` is the UI analog of `objectExtensions`; the app is a shell with group anchors.
- #14553 ruling (2026-09-02, option B, PR #14920): a contribution aimed at a missing group is relocated and reported at `warn` and at build time, never refused, because the fold is order-independent and the contributing package may be optional.
- #27928 ruling record 6566915346 (letter E): no key is added to any nav item; the served `navigation` stays as declared.
- #32585 / ADR-0019 D3 as amended 2026-11-12: a suite may surface several apps, each defined by a different package (the Salesforce shape).
- The `homePageId` tombstone (`HOME_PAGE_ID_RETIRED`, same file): an id into `navigation` with no referential integrity, resolved by a silent fallback, is the condemned shape.

## Protocol declaration

A, B and D change the authorable contract (`Clause-②: yes (widening)`, `Metadata-protocol: added` for A and D; B changes a refusal's door). C changes nothing.

## Premises, with re-check commands

1. Part (2) of the card is already expressible. Every nav entry carries `order` ("Sort order within the same level"), the fold keeps a contributed item as authored, and the console sorts each level by `order` after the fold. A contributed entry with an `order` between two of the app's numbered entries is drawn between them. An app that numbers none of its entries (all sort as 0) gives a module only "before all" or "after all", which is the app allowing or not allowing interleaving. A contribution's `items` is an array of `NavigationItemSchema`, so it may carry a `group` with children: the app need not pre-declare every group.
   - `grep -n "order: z.number" packages/spec/src/ui/app.zod.ts`
   - `grep -n "group.children.push\|nav.push" packages/objectql/src/registry.ts`
   - `grep -n "sort(byNavOrder)" ui/packages/layout/src/NavigationRenderer.tsx`
   - Read, not run. The dispatch order owes a pin test.
2. HotCRM 6.2.1 numbers none of its app entries: `grep -c "order:" src/sales/apps/crm.app.ts` in hotcrm answers 0. Interleaving into the upstream app needs upstream to number its entries once (a hotcrm card).
3. The console half needs no change for any option that puts the entry in the served trees and the landing in the served app: `resolveDeclaredLandingRoute` reads both from the served app.
4. No cross-package nav-id uniqueness check exists; `findEntryById` takes the first match, the app's own entries first.

## Options

| | What it does | What the customer feels | Work |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| A | Seat's A: the app's `landing` may name a contributed entry (checked after the fold) and a contribution may declare `before` / `after` an app entry id. | Both asks answered. Two positioning vocabularies (`order` and `before`/`after`) for one job. | spec + objectql + cli + ui ordering, 3 to 4 PRs. Precedents: #14920 (+1275/−47) for the post-fold check, #28449 (+595/−31) for a new key; console ordering has no precedent. |
| B | Seat's B: the app's `landing` may name any entry of the folded navigation. The dangling-id refusal moves from parse to the post-fold doors (`os build` / `os validate` over the artifact, the registry fold). | A typo is reported later than today, and at runtime only as a warning. Disabling the module leaves the landing dangling: the reader silently opens somewhere else. The upstream app does not know the module's ids, so the customer still edits the upstream app's `landing` and replays it on every sync. | spec + objectql + cli, 2 PRs. Precedent #14920 (+1275/−47). |
| C | No change. | A module's entry becomes a landing only by being first in the order, or by the module shipping its own app (ADR-0019 D3 as amended; HotCRM's Service app). "A rep lands on Sales Orders inside the CRM app" stays unanswered. | none |
| D | New in this evaluation: the contribution carries the landing. `navigationContributions[].landing` reuses `AppLandingEntrySchema`; each `item` must be one of that contribution's own `items`, refused at parse otherwise. The fold appends contributed landing entries after the app's own, by `priority`, and drops a disabled package's with its entries. | The module says which audience opens on its entry. A typo is refused when saved. Disabling the module removes entry and landing together, so nothing dangles. No upstream edit. The app's own landing is asked first, so the app owner keeps the last word. | spec + objectql, 1 to 2 PRs. Precedent #28449 (+595/−31) for the spec half; the fold half has no precedent (one register field, one append). No console change (premise 3). |

Business reading: A is "let the tenant's shop sign hang anywhere and also let the landlord's directory point at it"; B is "the landlord's directory lists a tenant by name and goes stale when the tenant leaves"; C is "tenants get their own front door or none"; D is "each tenant hangs its own sign on the space it rents".

## Recommendation: D, with part (2) answered by `order` (docs and a pin, no new key)

End state by axis ① alone: in two years an app is a shell that several packages fill, and each package describes only what it brings. ADR-0130 §1.5 already draws that seam for navigation; D keeps the landing on the same side of it, B crosses it in the other direction (the base naming its extension's id). Odoo modules and Dynamics solution layers model it the same way: the extension declares its own entry and where it sits. The Salesforce shape (app plus profile assignment by the admin, or one app per module) is option C's second route and stays available.

- A not taken: `before` / `after` duplicates `order` (premise 1); it revives #28022's B with no new evidence.
- B not taken: it moves a loud parse refusal to a later, weaker door, creates a dangling state on disable, and leaves the card's own complaint (editing the upstream app) in place.
- C not taken: the one-app case has real pull and the workaround (order as landing) is the idiom #28022 was ruled to end.

Self-check: by ① alone the letter is D; ②③④ flip it: no. ② one downstream project (p3), so it queues behind p1/p2 work, timing only. ③ D refuses at save, B reports later and falls back quietly at runtime. ④ D adds one optional key, a permanent obligation; B adds no key but a diagnostic vocabulary and three check sites. Work differs by less than 3×.

Confidence gaps: the downstream card (steedos-labs/os-project-blackcat-crm#70) is outside this session's access, so whether the customer owns the app or copies the upstream one is inferred from #33234. Premise 1 is read, not run. D's known limit: when the app itself declares a landing for the same audience, the app wins and the module cannot override it.

## After the ruling

The spec seat returns the card to `pm:queue` and dispatches. For D: (1) spec: `NavigationContributionSchema.landing`, its parse refusal, liveness row with its reader in the same PR, the `AppLandingEntrySchema` docblock sentence "cannot be named here" rewritten to point at the contribution's key; (2) objectql: the registry stores and folds contributed landing entries after the app's own, by priority, skipping a disabled package; (3) docs and one pin for premise 1 (`order` on a contributed entry, a contributed group); (4) a hotcrm card to number the CRM app's entries if upstream wants modules to interleave. `before` / `after` is not built under B, C or D.

os-decision-facets
① Long-term soundness: D keeps one rule (a landing and its target live in one package, checked at parse); B adds a second validation time for the same key; A adds a second positioning vocabulary.
② Business pull: one downstream project today (#33234, 10 accounts measured); p3.
③ AI-error proofing: D is a loud refusal at save; B is a later report and a quiet runtime fallback, the `homePageId` shape.
④ No proliferation: C adds nothing; D adds one optional key; B adds a diagnostic code and three check sites; A adds both a key and the checks.
Prior rulings read: "landing contributed entry navigationContributions", "navigationContributions position", "navigation contribution order between entries" → 15 / 22 / 20 hits, read #28022 (6545223246), #14553 (PR #14920), #27928 (6566915346), #32585; ADR-0130 §1.5, ADR-0029 D7, ADR-0019 D3; thread: none

## Seat: closed not planned under the maintainer's ruling C · 2026-11-14T21:23Z

⛔ Not a claim.

- **Ruling-ref:** Leehom chose C 「不改」 at 2026-11-14T21:19:19Z (decision thread `cmsg_01TenzsRopZj4jMbvjX8uz1XKbi11aY8SWRcPc43gTa4HY`, card `cmsg_01TenzsRopZj4jMbvjX8uz1X2urAufVvk5hC7JsAsmxj3R`, choice record read by the seat on that thread: option index 3, chosen by the maintainer). Record on this card: 6884379643. `needs-user-decision` leaves with this comment; the body carries the `Ruled:` line.
- **Part (1), landing on a contributed entry:** not built. An app's `landing` names only its own entries (#28022 record 6545223246, letter A, stands). A module whose audience needs its own landing ships its own app.
- **Part (2), placing a contributed entry between the app's own:** the seat confirmed the evaluation's reading against `main` (read, not run). `applyNavContributions` (`packages/objectql/src/registry.ts` ~:10842) pushes a contribution's `items` as authored, `order` included, and the console sorts each level by `order` after the fold (`ui/packages/layout/src/navOrder.ts#byNavOrder`: top level, each group's children, mobile tab bar). A contributed entry with `order: 25` lands between the app's `20` and `30`. It needs the app to number its own entries; unnumbered entries all sort as `0`, so a contribution stays after them. **For the downstream filer:** this is available on 18.4.0 today, with no new key; the upstream app has to number its entries (HotCRM 6.2.1 numbers none).
- **Docs gap filed:** #33447 (p3, spec lane): the `navigationContributions` docs never say this, and a pin that the fold keeps `order`.
- **State:** closed `not_planned`. Reopening is free; the maintainer can overrule.
